children: China is unlikely to roll out large-scale policy support despite weak factory activity data in October, according to BofA Securities in a research note. China's official purchasing managers' index fell into contraction territory last month and missed market expectations, the bank points out. However, BofA continues to believe that "policymakers are unlikely to pivot decisively toward supporting domestic demand unless export growth slows meaningfully". The coming October trade data will be key to assessing whether the deterioration in purchasing managers' index export orders signals a broader slowdown in exports, the bank says. (tracy.qu@wsj.com)
